subject.title: [Bug]: Windows Scheduled Task gateway restart/health becomes inconsistent after ready

question: Should this remain the canonical live issue for the remaining Windows Scheduled Task post-ready/relaunch instability, or should maintainers split/retire it in favor of narrower open Windows restart issues?
rationale: Current main has partial fixes, but the remaining behavior needs maintainer judgment and live Windows proof because multiple narrower issues and an open candidate PR now overlap the same surface.

options.title: Keep As Canonical
options.body: Leave this issue open as the umbrella until the remaining Windows Scheduled Task restart/health path has maintainer-reviewed live proof.

options.title: Split To Narrow Issues
options.body: Close this only after explicitly moving the remaining evidence to a narrower canonical issue such as the schtasks relaunch or foreground-listener report.

options.title: Resolve Via Candidate PR
options.body: Treat the open candidate PR as sufficient only if it gains maintainer-approved proof that covers this issue's broader post-ready instability, not just its narrower sibling.

recommendation.title: Keep As Canonical
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open as the umbrella until the remaining Windows Scheduled Task restart/health path has maintainer-reviewed live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is assigned here and has the strongest recent Windows gateway restart history in the inspected evidence.
